TN-2025-HB1369.s: This law requires the health department to make blood lead level testing available for children before they attend public schools and for pregnant women who get WIC food vouchers. If a child or pregnant woman has high lead levels or lead poisoning, the law calls for extra health, school, nutrition, and other support services. It also requires juvenile detention facilities that get federal money to help juveniles in custody who have high lead levels or lead poisoning.

TN-2025-HB1455.s: The act would make it a crime to train artificial intelligence to encourage suicide or homicide, give emotional support, act like a companion, pose as a health worker, or simulate a human being. It also lets harmed people sue and seek damages, including $150,000 in liquidated damages, attorney's fees, and court orders to stop use until the problem is fixed. The law takes effect July 1, 2026, and applies to conduct on or after that date.

TN-2025-HB162.s: This enacted law lets a county or city that charges property tax pay a property tax refund owed to a taxpayer in yearly installments, with each payment counted as a credit on future property tax bills, if certain rules are met. It applies through June 30, 2041. It also lets an annual report be sent in electronic form to the state board of equalization.

TN-2025-HB1666.s: As enacted, the law extends the same protections and duties that already apply to the use of sex-based pronouns to the use of sex-based honorifics, such as titles. It applies to state government, public schools, local school systems, and public colleges and their students, teachers, employees, and contractors. The law took effect when it became law.

TN-2025-HB1733.s: As enacted, the law creates a criminal offense for certain school employees who intentionally bully or cyberbully a student. It also says a teacher or school employee found to have done harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying can be dismissed or suspended. The law applies to acts on or after July 1, 2026.

TN-2025-HB1817.s: The law changes rules for commercial drivers who cannot read and speak English well enough to handle traffic signs, talk with the public, and fill out required reports. If an officer finds this during a safety check, the driver can be put out of service, the truck cannot keep going until a qualified substitute driver arrives, and the driver’s commercial license can be suspended until the driver passes a state English test. The employer is responsible for fines or fees tied to the suspension or getting the license back, and a violation is a Class C misdemeanor with a $500 fine for the employer. Parts of the law took effect when it became law, and the rest takes effect January 1, 2027.

TN-2025-HB1878.s: This law changes rules for industrial development corporations in Tennessee. It lets a corporation’s board start a merger with another corporation, using the process for public benefit corporations. It took effect when it became law.

TN-2025-HB1906.s: As enacted, the law lets certain public workers count time spent on temporary disability as retirement service credit. For state police officers and some Tennessee Bureau of Investigation agents, that credit must be free to the worker if they apply on or after July 1, 2026. Local governments that pass a resolution may also offer this credit to their employees, and can choose to make it free for police officers; the act took effect July 1, 2026.

TN-2025-HB1967.s: This law changes penalties for leaving the scene of an accident. It makes a violation a Class E felony, and it makes it a Class D felony if a person fails to stop or follow the law after an accident when they knew or should have known someone died. It takes effect July 1, 2026.

TN-2025-HB2085.s: As enacted, this law changes a state finance rule by replacing a 30-day deadline with 45 days in Tennessee code. It also took effect when it became law.

TN-2025-HB2091.s: As enacted, the law sets a fee schedule for permits to operate off-highway vehicles at North Cumberland Wildlife Management Area. It also requires the director to post on the commission’s website the areas in Tennessee that allow off-highway motor vehicles, along with each area’s acreage and an estimated trail length. The act took effect when it became law.

TN-2025-HB2174.s: Tennessee’s law changes the rules for judges carrying weapons during judicial proceedings. It updates the judge exemption and says sitting or retired chancery, circuit, or appellate court judges, and governor-appointed judges, may carry a weapon, including a firearm, in places and ways allowed for law enforcement officers if they are allowed to carry a handgun. It took effect when it became law.

TN-2025-HB2204.s: The law requires TACIR, a state research group, to study pay and other benefits for state and local law enforcement officers in Tennessee and to report its findings by January 31, 2027. The study must look at how pay and benefits affect hiring and keeping officers, especially in smaller city and county departments, and at how state pay changes affect local officers. It also lets the safety commissioner set a hazardous duty label for highway patrol members that may be used for extra pay.

TN-2025-HB2320.s: The law updates the rules for convention center authorities in Tennessee and renames the act as the Convention Center and Agricultural Exposition Authorities Act. It changes a reporting rule so that, by January 1 each year, a copy of the report and annual audit must be filed with the city or town government that allowed the authority to form. It took effect when it became law.

TN-2025-HB2502.s: The law says money transfers from Tennessee to a place outside the United States or its territories are a taxable service, and the tax is based on the amount sent. It also sets up a special fund for that tax money and splits it among the state general fund, counties and metro governments for capital and infrastructure, teacher pay increases or bonuses, and extra pay for certain law enforcement officers. Most parts of the law take effect on January 1, 2027, while rule-making can start when the law takes effect.

TN-2025-HB2518.s: As enacted, this law affects state recycling work in Tennessee. It adds an annual report requirement for the departments of general services and environment and conservation, and they must send their findings to the General Assembly by December 31 each year. The title says it also sets up an office of cooperative marketing for recyclables and a recycling market development and diversion advisory council.

TN-2025-HB2533.s: Tennessee enacted changes to state education law that affect school funding rules, staff leave rules, agency structure, and school complaint handling. It says a local education agency or public charter school Title VI coordinator must review certain antisemitic discrimination or harassment complaints before they are sent on, and it bars parents from using some IEA money for ABLE Act account deposits. The law was signed on May 21, 2026 and takes effect July 1, 2026.

TN-2025-HB2592.s: As enacted, the law changes rules for electric utilities that serve areas outside their home city limits. It requires the utility board to expand so people from those outside areas have representation on the board. It also lets a required report be sent electronically.

TN-2025-HB2634.s: For Millington, this act raises the residency rule for people who want to run for mayor or alderman. A candidate would have to be a qualified voter and have lived in the city for at least one year before the election, instead of 60 days for mayor. It would take effect only if the city’s governing body approves it, and it became Private Chapter 32.

TN-2025-HB2649.s: For Bristol, the law updates how city council and school board members are chosen so all city voters can vote for all seats, with some seats tied to districts and others open to any city resident. It also shortens the time for new ordinances to take effect from 17 days to 7 days, changes the city’s property tax due dates, and sets up a city department of education. The changes affect Bristol city government, the board of education, property owners, and residents who vote in city elections.

TN-2025-HB659.s: As enacted, the law lets a county election commission set aside restroom facilities in a building where an election is held for campaign workers or volunteers. These workers may use those restrooms if they stay out of the polling place, and they must cover or remove campaign clothing before entering the marked area. It took effect July 1, 2025.

TN-2025-SB1255.s: The law requires the health department to make blood lead level testing available for pregnant women who get vouchers through the WIC food program. If a woman has high lead levels or lead poisoning, the department must provide special nutrition help, education on lowering lead in the body, and other services for those cases. It also requires testing and follow-up steps for children before public school attendance and for certain youth in juvenile detention facilities.

TN-2025-SB1587.s: As enacted, this law makes it an offense for a person who is unlawfully present in the United States to drive a commercial motor vehicle in Tennessee, and for someone to knowingly let that happen. If a person is arrested for that offense, the local law enforcement agency must make sure federal immigration authorities are told. It also lets injured people, the attorney general, and private whistleblowers bring civil cases for harm tied to that driving, with damages, fines, and court costs; it takes effect July 1, 2026.

TN-2025-SB1602.s: Starting July 1, 2026, this law changes Tennessee penalties for leaving the scene of an accident. Failing to stop after an accident becomes a Class E felony, and it becomes a Class D felony if the driver knew or should have known that someone died. It affects people who do not stop or follow the rules after a crash.

TN-2025-SB1622.s: This law requires the Department of Children’s Services commissioner to create a statewide quality assurance program that uses monitoring, review, and feedback to track how services are working for children and families. The program must include county-level review groups, a state office and committee, and a public website grade for each county that is updated at least every six months. The commissioner must also send quarterly progress reports starting with the fiscal quarter ending September 30, 2026, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.

TN-2025-SB1665.s: As enacted, this law says the same protections and duties that apply when using a pronoun tied to a person's sex also apply when using an honorific tied to that person's sex. It affects the state, state workers, public schools, local school systems, public college and university students, teachers, employees, and contractors. It took effect when it became law on May 22, 2026.

TN-2025-SB1713.s: This law requires leaders of state, county, city, metro, and public college systems to file a yearly statement with the comptroller starting January 1, 2027. The statement says they have not used a rule that gives a discriminatory preference to increase diversity, equity, or inclusion. It also lets the attorney general do related investigations.

TN-2025-SB1748.s: As enacted, this law changes rules for commercial drivers who cannot read and speak English well enough to handle road signs, public questions, and required reports. It lets officers issue an out-of-service order during a safety check, suspends the driver’s commercial license, and requires a state test before the license can be reinstated, with some exceptions for drivers who cannot meet a hearing standard but have an exemption. The employer is liable for fines and fees, and the law takes effect for most purposes on January 1, 2027.

TN-2025-SB1774.s: As enacted, this law creates a criminal offense for school employees who intentionally bully or cyberbully a student. It also says a teacher or other school employee found to have done harassment, intimidation, bullying, or cyberbullying can be dismissed or suspended. The law applies to acts on or after July 1, 2026.

TN-2025-SB2040.s: As enacted, the law says a pharmacy benefits manager, or PBM, cannot own or control a pharmacy in Tennessee starting January 1, 2027. It also requires pharmacy license holders to give the state pharmacy board yearly ownership and control details, and the board can deny, suspend, or revoke a license for false or missing information. The law lets the board issue limited-use licenses for certain hard-to-get drugs, and that part ends on September 1, 2028.

TN-2025-SB2102.s: The law changes rules for electric utilities that serve customers outside their home city limits. It requires those utilities to expand their boards so people in the outside area have a seat on the board. It also lets a required report be sent in electronically.

TN-2025-SB2162.s: Tennessee law now lets a governing body hold a closed meeting to interview people for director-level staff jobs without giving public notice first. No final decision can be made in that closed meeting; any vote must happen later in an open meeting. The meeting minutes must list who was there, with limits on who may attend, and some job applications and interviews may stay private if requested.

TN-2025-SB2227.s: As enacted, this law makes several changes to Tennessee health rules. It revises some reporting requirements, requires people licensed by the psychology board to complete suicide prevention training, and defines palliative care as comfort-focused care for serious illness. It also clarifies the rulemaking power of health boards and the health commissioner, and it took effect when it became law.

TN-2025-SB2228.s: As enacted, this law makes many changes to Tennessee education rules. It blocks parents from using certain education savings funds to put money into an ABLE account, and it requires local schools to first look into reported antisemitic discrimination and harassment complaints before sending them to the state education coordinator. It also changes rules for school staff leave, school and agency names, and which education-related groups and contracts are covered by state law.

TN-2025-SB2385.s: The law changes how Tennessee defines students who are "economically disadvantaged," a term for students from lower-income or certain high-need groups. It also tells the education department to ask the federal government to change the state plan so more students can be counted through direct certification, which means they are found eligible without a household form. Starting with the 2027-2028 school year, school districts that lose funding because fewer students are counted in this group can get extra state money to keep their weighted TISA funding level the same, and that rule ends July 1, 2030.

TN-2025-SB2452.s: The law allows alcoholic drinks and beer to be served and consumed at certain private events without a state alcohol license, if no one under 21 is served. It also requires the event owner or operator to show proof that they took reasonable steps to keep alcohol from people under 21. The act took effect on May 22, 2026.

TN-2025-SB2693.s: The law changes the residency rule for Millington mayor candidates. A person must now live in the city for one year before the election, instead of 60 days, to run for mayor. It only takes effect if Millington's local government approves it by a two-thirds vote.

TN-2025-SB2713.s: The measure changes Sardis town rules, but only if the town government approves it by a two-thirds vote. It updates the town charter by removing old language, letting the board set salaries and meeting dates by ordinance, and changing the mayor and aldermen terms from two years to four years. It also changes who can vote in town elections and says local voters living in the town may vote, while some nonresidents who own land in the town may also vote under set rules.

TN-2025-SB539.s: As enacted, the law sets rules for how multi-unit rental housing with government low-income use limits is assessed for property tax. It tells assessors how to value this housing, including how to treat rent limits and low-income housing tax credits. Owners must tell the property assessor when the property is covered by these limits, when that status ends, or when foreclosure starts. These rules take effect January 1, 2026, for most purposes, with some parts taking effect when the law became effective.

TN-2026114S2-HB7001.s: The law changes Tennessee election rules for the 2026 congressional elections. It says one state election rule will not apply to the 2026 primary election for U.S. representative, and it took effect when it became law on May 7, 2026.

TN-2026114S2-HB7005.s: Makes money available for lawful expenses of Tennessee’s Second Extraordinary Session of the 114th General Assembly, including staff, daily pay, travel, and other session costs. It also sets aside funds tied to other parts of the session, including a possible elections bill if that measure becomes law. It became law on May 7, 2026.

TN-2026114S2-SB7001.s: As enacted, this law makes changes to Tennessee election rules for the 2026 congressional elections. It says one election rule will not apply to the 2026 primary election for U.S. representative. The law took effect when it became law.

TN-2026114S2-SB7005.s: As enacted, the bill provides money for lawful expenses of the Tennessee General Assembly’s second extraordinary session, including staff, daily pay, travel, and other costs. It also sets aside funds for other session-related needs and for a possible elections bill if that bill becomes law. The act took effect when it became law.
